evidence.claim: The India country sheet says the richest 10% held 57% of national income, the poorest 50% held 13%, and the richest 1% held 22%, describing India as poor and very unequal.
evidence.title: Page 24 - World Inequality Report 2022
evidence.excerpt: The India country sheet says the richest 10% held 57% of national income, the poorest 50% held 13%, and the richest 1% held 22%, describing India as poor and very unequal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative inequality report with a precise country sheet and widely cited figures.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline and close-in context for the 2022 period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution only; the figures reflect structural inequality and long-run distribution, not a single-year executive choice.
contrary_evidence: The figures are from 2021, so they are baseline context rather than a 2022 policy outcome.
The report does not isolate Modi-specific causation.

evidence.claim: India launched Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 on 7 February 2022 to enhance Universal Immunization Programme coverage across 416 districts in 33 states and union territories after a pandemic-era fall in DPT3 coverage.
evidence.title: Reaching life-saving vaccines to all
evidence.excerpt: India launched Intensified Mission Indradhanush 4.0 on 7 February 2022 to enhance Universal Immunization Programme coverage across 416 districts in 33 states and union territories after a pandemic-era fall in DPT3 coverage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent WHO feature story with dated 2022 policy and rollout details; strong corroboration for government immunization action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s health policy, though implementation depended on states and frontline workers.
contrary_evidence: The source emphasizes coverage catch-up after a pandemic backslide, not a completed outcome.
It documents a launch and rollout plan more than final measured gains.

evidence.claim: The ministry reorganized its welfare work into Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti, and Mission Vatsalya; 40,000 Saksham Anganwadis were identified in FY 2022-23 and more than 15 crore Poshan Maah activities were conducted.
evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.excerpt: The ministry reorganized its welfare work into Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti, and Mission Vatsalya; 40,000 Saksham Anganwadis were identified in FY 2022-23 and more than 15 crore Poshan Maah activities were conducted.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary year-end ministry review with concrete scheme redesign and implementation counts.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period child and women welfare policy evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s social-policy choices, though field delivery depended on states and local workers.
contrary_evidence: The source is a ministry self-report.
Scheme restructuring and event counts do not by themselves prove improved nutrition or protection outcomes.

evidence.claim: eShram had more than 28.5 crore registered workers, ESIC launched an online maternity-claim portal for 58.69 lakh insured women, and the ministry reported 2,297 job fairs in 2022.
evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Ministry of Labour and Employment
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Labour & Employment
evidence.excerpt: eShram had more than 28.5 crore registered workers, ESIC launched an online maternity-claim portal for 58.69 lakh insured women, and the ministry reported 2,297 job fairs in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with large-scale labor-protection and service-delivery figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s labor policy and digital social-protection infrastructure.
contrary_evidence: Registry counts and job fairs do not by themselves prove job quality or income gains.
The source is a ministry self-report rather than independent evaluation.

evidence.claim: PMGKAY continued through Phase VII in 2022 with about 1,118 LMT foodgrains allocated in total, and ONORC exceeded 93 crore portability transactions delivering more than 177 LMT of foodgrains.
evidence.title: Year-End Review of Department of Food and Public Distribution– 2022
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
evidence.excerpt: PMGKAY continued through Phase VII in 2022 with about 1,118 LMT foodgrains allocated in total, and ONORC exceeded 93 crore portability transactions delivering more than 177 LMT of foodgrains.
evidence.source_locator: PMGKAY and One Nation One Ration Card sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry review with specific program totals and beneficiary-access metrics.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 target-period food-security and portability evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s food-security policy, with fair-price-shop and state execution shared across levels of government.
contrary_evidence: This is emergency and food-security relief, not proof of long-run food-system resilience.
Administrative distribution totals do not directly show household nutrition quality.

evidence.claim: The ministry reported that 26.37 lakh tribal students received scholarships through DBT from 1 April to 31 December 2022, and the Cabinet approved Rs 28,920 crore for 452 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools, upgrades to 211 existing schools, and 15 centres of excellence for sports.
evidence.title: Year End Review 2022: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Tribal Affairs
evidence.excerpt: The ministry reported that 26.37 lakh tribal students received scholarships through DBT from 1 April to 31 December 2022, and the Cabinet approved Rs 28,920 crore for 452 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools, upgrades to 211 existing schools, and 15 centres of excellence for sports.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry year-end review with clear distribution and institution-building figures for a vulnerable group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s tribal policy, with some delivery through state and school systems.
contrary_evidence: Scholarship counts do not prove completion or learning outcomes.
The EMRS approval is a long-term investment, not an immediate welfare result.

evidence.claim: The department said it sought to build an inclusive society for persons with disabilities and in 2022 held sign-language events at 3,200 places, signed MoUs with Amazon and Flipkart for skills and employment pathways, and expanded rehabilitation services through new and upgraded centres.
evidence.title: Year End Review- 2022 of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India / Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
evidence.excerpt: The department said it sought to build an inclusive society for persons with disabilities and in 2022 held sign-language events at 3,200 places, signed MoUs with Amazon and Flipkart for skills and employment pathways, and expanded rehabilitation services through new and upgraded centres.
evidence.source_locator: opening summary and major achievements sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary ministry review with concrete inclusion and employment-program details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s disability policy, though effects depend on state and private-sector follow-through.
contrary_evidence: Event counts and MoUs do not by themselves prove broad access or equal opportunity.
The ministry framing is self-reported and likely optimistic.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2022 evidence of a Modi-directed command-and-control reform, custody audit, launch-readiness change, or internal NCA practice change.
Personal attribution is thin for the more favorable multilateral statements and nuclear-governance positions.
The Russia balancing record is mostly government-level and UN-mission level rather than a clearly documented personal decision by Modi on oil, abstentions, or summit sequencing.
There is no 2022 external-combat or proxy-war exposure to test civilian-protection or proxy-control lenses in a strong way.
Direct Modi-level incitement evidence is thinner than the broader BJP and state-level abuse record.
The strongest custody-death and abuse claims still rely on NGO and U.S. State Department reporting with mixed central/state attribution.
Direct evidence of Modi personally directing electoral manipulation is thin relative to the stronger party-level and institutional record.
Several items show contestability and oversight but do not themselves prove that Modi strengthened democratic institutions in 2022.
Household-level and median-welfare evidence is thinner than the macro, capex, and program-count evidence.
Corruption, favoritism, and politically connected business privilege are underdeveloped relative to investment and growth material.
Independent outcome measures and subnational equity checks are still thin relative to the many ministry self-reports.
The current record is strong on inputs and service counts but weak on durable quality, learning, nutrition, and sustained poverty improvement.
No audited evidence of direct personal falsehood, correction, or hidden conflicts of interest has been recovered for 2022.
The negative items are mostly institutional opacity or noncooperation, not direct proof of personal self-dealing or a documented lie by Modi.
Project-level outcome audits and durability checks are still thinner than the program-design and rollout material.
Direct evidence that Modi replaced a specific ineffective implementer is absent.
